title: Contingent Corporate Bill-Audit & Tax-Credit Recovery — Operator Companion Workbook
subtitle: 6 Printable Operator Worksheets for Counterparty Underwriting, Recovery Economics, Evidence-Led Execution, Statutory Controls, Carrier and Utility Automation, and a Transferable Small-Team Recovery Pod

worksheets.title: Arbitrage Deal / Counterparty Underwriting & Spread Qualification
worksheets.purpose: Qualify recoverable corporate expenses before purchasing specialist time. Separate measurable carrier, utility, property-assessment, and employment-credit opportunities from speculative savings; establish account authority, contract eligibility, evidence quality, collection timing, and an operator fee that survives both disputes and delivery costs.
instructions: Create one opportunity record for each client entity, account, recovery category, and assessment or invoice period. Obtain signed authority and immutable baseline invoices before sharing findings, contacting counterparties, or requesting access to client account systems.

Read the actual carrier agreement, utility tariff, assessment notice, or credit statute before applying a recovery percentage. Record exclusions, waivers, filing windows, account ownership, and specialist requirements; never substitute a public marketing page for the governing document.

Estimate recoverable value from a documented sample and distinguish issued credits from merely alleged errors. Model the operator's contractual share separately from client benefits, then subtract specialist delivery costs and expected rework before qualifying the spread.

Interview accounts payable, procurement, facilities, payroll, and the authorized tax practitioner as relevant. Reconcile their answers against documents, identify incumbent auditors, and assign ownership for duplicate claims, prior appeals, disputed baselines, and delayed counterparty responses.

Advance only opportunities with an identified payer, defensible entitlement, accessible evidence, and executable fee terms. Route tax-linked compensation for practitioner review independently of commercial bill auditing, and document a narrower paid-processing scope when contingent compensation is restricted.

fields.name: Client entity, account map, and signing authority
fields.prompt: Identify the contracting entity, covered subsidiaries, account numbers, authorized signer, and records custodian. Explain how authority will be verified and which accounts remain outside the signed engagement until separately documented.
fields.example: Harbor Components LLC covers two facilities and parcel accounts ending 1842 and 9916. Its controller signs the engagement and account-specific Letters of Authorization. A third facility belongs to Harbor Realty LLC and stays excluded until that entity signs. Accounts payable provides twelve months of dated invoice exports.

fields.name: Recovery lane and counterparty entitlement
fields.prompt: Specify the recoverable charge, governing entitlement, counterparty responsible for resolution, and recovery period. Distinguish historical refunds, prospective tariff savings, assessment reductions, and tax credits because their evidence and fee treatments differ.
fields.example: The initial lane is duplicate utility demand billing for meters A104 and A105, not general energy procurement. Twelve invoices show $42,000 of potentially duplicated charges. The municipal utility's billing supervisor receives the evidence package; prospective tariff changes require a separate baseline schedule and savings calculation.

fields.name: Baseline integrity and sample extrapolation
fields.prompt: Describe the invoice population, sample selection method, excluded periods, duplicate removal, and reconciliation controls. Show how the sample supports a qualified estimate without presenting extrapolated recoveries as approved credits or earned revenue.
fields.example: A sample of 500 shipments from 10,000 annual shipments contains $1,200 of apparent billing errors. Multiplying by twenty suggests $24,000 for screening only. The analyst stratifies by service, month, and account before expanding review; the proposal labels $24,000 as an estimate requiring shipment-level validation.

fields.name: Carrier guarantees, waivers, and claim windows
fields.prompt: Record the exact FedEx or UPS contract provision, service eligibility, effective dates, exclusions, filing deadline, and authorized submission method. Separate delivery-guarantee requests from duplicate-charge or rating disputes, which may follow different contractual procedures.
fields.example: The illustrative parcel agreement waives delivery-guarantee refunds for negotiated services but preserves billing-error disputes. The analyst excludes late-delivery claims and reviews duplicate charges instead. A contract-specific deadline register records each invoice's last submission date; the pod does not apply one carrier's timing rule to another account.

fields.name: Utility, waste, and telecom tariff fit
fields.prompt: Identify the operative tariff or service schedule, physical equipment supporting eligibility, required meter evidence, and contract-change mechanism. Explain whether savings arise from a billing correction, a new rate election, or a measurable service reduction.
fields.example: A facility's cooling-tower deduction requires a qualifying submeter and accepted readings under the local sewer schedule. Historical invoices alone cannot prove evaporation volume. The operator collects installation records and monthly readings, then distinguishes a $9,600 refund request from a prospective $800 monthly charge reduction.

fields.name: Property assessment appeal qualification
fields.prompt: Capture parcel ownership, jurisdiction, assessment date, appeal deadline, representation requirements, and valuation evidence. Separate assessed-value reductions from actual tax savings and identify other advisers whose existing engagement could create overlapping compensation.
fields.example: A Texas warehouse has an $8,000,000 assessment and a supported $7,400,000 comparison value. At an illustrative 2.2% combined rate, the potential annual tax difference is $13,200, not $600,000. A qualified local representative checks the notice, filing deadline, existing engagement, and applicable licensing requirements before submission.

fields.name: WOTC cohort eligibility and processing scope
fields.prompt: Identify hiring dates, applicable statutory authorization, targeted-group documentation, certification workflow, and practitioner responsibilities. Keep employer tax benefits separate from processing revenue and state the permitted fee basis before promising a credit-linked compensation arrangement.
fields.example: A historical 2025 cohort contains 100 employees whose certification records require review. The operator charges an agreed $100 per completed processing file, yielding $10,000 if all deliverables qualify for billing. For later hiring dates, the practitioner verifies any enacted extension of 26 U.S.C. §51(c)(4) before activating screening.

fields.name: Contingency spread and retained share
fields.prompt: Calculate the operator's fee from eligible client recoveries, then deduct direct specialist and delivery costs. State the contractual earning event, collection trigger, dispute allocation, and minimum acceptable contribution for the proposed engagement.
fields.example: An $80,000 eligible utility refund at a 35% retained share produces $28,000 of operator revenue. Specialist work costs $7,500 and evidence preparation costs $2,500, leaving $18,000 before shared overhead. The agreement earns the fee on an accepted, applied client credit and invoices after supporting proof arrives.

fields.name: Counterparty timing and collection confidence
fields.prompt: Assess counterparty responsiveness, historical processing duration, client payment behavior, disputed amounts, and escalation contacts. Convert these observations into a dated collection range rather than treating an accepted recovery as immediately available operating cash.
fields.example: The municipal utility estimates sixty days to review the package and thirty additional days to apply an accepted credit. The client then pays the operator within fifteen days. The cash plan therefore allows 105 days from submission, while the claim ledger separately tracks acceptance, application, invoicing, and payment.

fields.name: Qualification decision and disqualifying conditions
fields.prompt: Summarize the evidence-based decision, unresolved dependencies, named owners, and latest acceptable resolution dates. Define objective conditions that stop work, including absent authority, expired deadlines, duplicate representation, uneconomic delivery, and unsupported benefit assumptions.
fields.example: Advance the $80,000 utility case after the controller signs both meter authorizations and the specialist confirms tariff entitlement. Exclude parcel guarantee claims because the agreement waives them. Stop additional utility analysis if documentary support falls below $35,000 of eligible recovery or specialist costs exceed the approved $7,500 budget without revised economics.

worksheets.completion_gate: The engagement owner signs a qualification record containing verified authority, baseline evidence, account-specific entitlement, deadline ownership, a documented fee basis, and positive delivery contribution. No excluded lane enters production merely because another lane qualified.

worksheets.title: Unit Economics, Escrow/Reserve Float & Working-Capital Calculator
worksheets.purpose: Translate recovery opportunities into recognized operator revenue, cash requirements, and owner profit without counting client bills or credits as sales. Reconcile all three canonical scenarios, model delayed collections, and isolate operating reserves from any client-owned funds or unearned fees.
instructions: Build separate schedules for historical recovery fees, verified monthly shared savings, and completed WOTC processing services. For every line, record client benefit, retained share or fixed price, recognition basis, invoice timing, cash receipt, and associated delivery expense.

Reproduce the canonical Conservative, Base, and Scaled totals exactly before testing sensitivities. Treat the illustrative channel mixes below as reconciling allocations rather than additional source forecasts; scenario changes must remain visibly separate from the canonical comparison.

Distinguish core recurring overhead from total expenses used to calculate owner net profit. Contractor delivery, specialist review, acquisition, rework, insurance, and transaction costs belong in the annual cost bridge even when omitted from a narrow monthly overhead estimate.

Model cash using collection dates rather than claim approval dates. Exclude client refund balances from available runway, document restricted reserve treatment, and use a weekly cash schedule to expose the combined effect of delayed refunds and contractor payment commitments.

Have the responsible accountant review principal-versus-agent treatment, variable consideration, and service completion evidence. A thirty-six-month shared-savings term establishes a measurement period; it does not permit booking all future monthly fees when the contract is signed.

fields.name: Recognized revenue perimeter and retained-share mapping
fields.prompt: Define what the operator controls and earns in each recovery lane. Identify client-owned amounts, retained_share assumptions, pass-through items, and the accountant's ASC 606 assessment so gross billings cannot inflate recognized operator revenue.
fields.example: For the Base allocation, retained_share equals 0.35 on $600,000 of eligible refunds and 0.40 on $600,000 of verified annual savings. These produce $210,000 and $240,000 of operator revenue. Completed processing adds $55,000. Client benefits and underlying utility or freight bills never become an extra revenue line.

fields.name: Conservative scenario reconciliation
fields.prompt: Reconcile annual revenue, expenses, owner net profit, margin, and staffing to the canonical Conservative case. Show the channel allocation explicitly and identify which costs are already included so they are not deducted twice.
fields.example: Illustrative allocation: $200,000 recovered at 30% yields $60,000; $100,000 verified savings at 40% yields $40,000; 100 processing files at $100 yield $10,000. Revenue totals $110,000. Expenses of $77,000 leave $33,000 owner net profit, exactly 30%, with one full-time employee and three contractors.

fields.name: Base scenario reconciliation
fields.prompt: Reconcile the Base case using distinct earned-fee streams and a complete annual expense bridge. Preserve the exact canonical profit and margin, and distinguish modeled annual delivery capacity from the number of people on the pod.
fields.example: Refund shares contribute $210,000, shared savings contribute $240,000, and 550 completed processing files at $100 contribute $55,000. The $505,000 total less $287,850 of expenses equals $217,150 owner net profit. Dividing $217,150 by $505,000 gives 43.0%. Staffing remains one full-time employee plus three contractors.

fields.name: Scaled small-team scenario reconciliation
fields.prompt: Reproduce the Scaled revenue, expense, margin, profit, and six-person staffing totals. Explain the operational capacity assumptions behind the illustration without suggesting that more client spending itself creates additional recognized operator revenue.
fields.example: Illustrative allocation: $1,000,000 refunded at 35% yields $350,000; $1,100,000 verified savings at 40% yields $440,000; 1,100 completed files at $100 yield $110,000. Revenue is $900,000. Expenses of $396,000 leave $504,000, or 56%, with two full-time employees and four contractors, totaling six people.

fields.name: Thirty-six-month shared-savings waterfall
fields.prompt: Specify the normalized baseline, measurement adjustments, monthly client savings, operator share, and thirty-six-month duration. Describe how closures, volume changes, tariff revisions, reversals, and termination affect each month's verified fee and recognition.
fields.example: Verified savings of $50,000 monthly at a 40% operator share produce a $20,000 monthly fee and $240,000 over twelve measured months. If sustained for all thirty-six months, fees total $720,000. Only earned periods enter current revenue; production-volume declines are normalized rather than mislabeled as tariff savings.

fields.name: Core overhead versus total expense bridge
fields.prompt: List recurring core overhead separately from variable delivery and other annual expenses. Reconcile the complete expense total to the selected scenario, keeping the published monthly operating range distinct from all-in costs of earning revenue.
fields.example: A Base illustration uses $6,500 monthly core overhead, or $78,000 annually. Add $125,000 contractor delivery, $35,000 acquisition, $25,000 specialist review, and $24,850 other operating costs. Total expenses equal $287,850. The $1,500–$9,500 monthly core range is therefore not a ceiling on total scenario expenses.

fields.name: Startup capital and delayed-collection runway
fields.prompt: Choose startup funding within the stated range and schedule setup spending, recurring burn, restricted reserves, and the first expected collection. Calculate remaining runway under a delayed-refund case without assuming unsigned deals provide usable cash.
fields.example: Start with $35,000, spend $4,500 on setup, and ring-fence $1,500 for fee reversals. Deployable cash is $29,000, supporting about 4.46 months at $6,500 core burn before variable costs. A seventy-five-day wait consumes $16,250 of core cash; committed specialist payments must be added separately.

fields.name: Client funds, reserve ownership, and release controls
fields.prompt: State who receives refunds, whether any client money enters operator accounts, and how reserves are funded and released. If custodial handling is proposed, identify the required contractual, banking, accounting, and jurisdiction-specific review before accepting funds.
fields.example: The utility pays an $80,000 refund directly to the client, and the operator invoices its earned $28,000 fee separately. A $1,500 operator-funded reversal reserve remains unavailable for routine spending until the documented exposure expires. Client refunds never finance payroll, and the operator offers no custodial account without a separately reviewed arrangement.

fields.name: Receivables aging and collection sensitivity
fields.prompt: Calculate average receivables using recognized fee revenue and collection duration, then compare the result with available working capital. Keep collection timing sensitivities separate from changes in entitlement, recognized revenue, and expected credit losses.
fields.example: The Base refund-fee stream averages $17,500 monthly from $210,000 annual revenue. At an illustrative sixty-day collection cycle, steady-state receivables approximate $35,000 using thirty-day months. At ninety days they approximate $52,500, requiring $17,500 more working capital before considering savings-fee receivables, tax-processing invoices, or overdue balances.

fields.name: Downside sensitivity and economic stop rule
fields.prompt: Stress a specific engagement for lower eligible recovery, higher specialist expense, and slower cash collection. Show contribution before overhead and define a documented decision rule without overwriting the three canonical annual scorecard scenarios.
fields.example: If the $80,000 utility estimate falls to $40,000, the 35% fee becomes $14,000. Original delivery costs of $10,000 leave $4,000 before overhead; an added $5,000 specialist requirement would make contribution negative $1,000. Pause incremental work and renegotiate scope rather than treating the original $28,000 fee estimate as collectible.

worksheets.completion_gate: The finance owner verifies exact canonical totals of $33,000, $217,150, and $504,000 annual owner net profit, signs the revenue-versus-client-benefit mapping, and confirms that dated operating commitments fit available operator cash without using client funds.

worksheets.title: End-to-End Execution, Idempotent Ledger & QA Pre-Flight Sheet
worksheets.purpose: Build a reproducible path from authorized invoice intake to collected operator fees. Use immutable evidence, deterministic claim identities, controlled state transitions, and independent review to prevent duplicate submissions, unsupported findings, premature invoicing, and silent mismatches between counterparty credits and client receipts.
instructions: Create an evidence manifest before extraction begins. Preserve each original file, calculate its SHA-256 digest, record account and period ownership, and link the signed authority so every proposed finding can be traced to an authorized source.

Normalize invoice identifiers, currencies, dates, and amounts while retaining raw source values. Use decimal arithmetic for money, distinguish credits from debits, and send ambiguous OCR output to a human queue instead of silently repairing material amounts.

Define the economic identity of each claim before writing submission automation. Enforce one active claim per identity, store attempts separately, and reconcile uncertain external responses before retrying; an internal idempotency key does not force a carrier endpoint to deduplicate.

Require an independent reviewer to compare entitlement, arithmetic, deadline, authority, and attached evidence before submission. Review every material exception and a documented sample of routine items, then preserve reviewer identity and decision timestamps in the event history.

Close work only after reconciling counterparty disposition, client credit application, fee earning, invoice issuance, and payment. Preserve denials and reversals as new events rather than rewriting history, and feed root causes back into qualification and extraction rules.

fields.name: Authorized intake manifest
fields.prompt: Define required source files, authorization links, ingestion timestamps, account ownership, and integrity checks. Explain how incomplete periods and documents received through unapproved channels are quarantined before any findings or submissions are produced.
fields.example: Manifest HC-UTIL-2025 lists twelve original PDF invoices, a meter schedule, the effective tariff, and two signed authorizations. Each file receives a SHA-256 digest and restricted storage key. November is initially missing, so the analyst requests it and marks that period incomplete instead of extrapolating a submission amount.

fields.name: Normalization and OCR exception rules
fields.prompt: Specify extraction fields, money precision, date formats, invoice reconciliation, and confidence thresholds. Identify which fields require visual confirmation and how the workflow preserves original values alongside normalized values for later reviewer inspection.
fields.example: The parser records account, invoice number, service dates, meter identifier, tariff code, quantity, rate, and tax. Decimal values quantize to cents only at the documented calculation step. An OCR reading of $18,800 against a $1,880 invoice total fails reconciliation and enters manual review with the source page attached.

fields.name: Deterministic claim identity and uniqueness
fields.prompt: Define the immutable components of a claim's economic identity and the database uniqueness constraint. Explain how corrections, resubmissions, and multiple distinct charge disputes on one invoice remain linked without creating duplicate recovery claims.
fields.example: A utility claim key combines tenant, counterparty, account, invoice, service period, charge line, and recovery reason. A unique database constraint permits one active claim for that identity. Correcting the requested amount from $920 to $890 creates a new version under the same claim, not another collectible asset.

fields.name: Ledger states and accounting boundaries
fields.prompt: List permitted claim states and the evidence needed for each transition. Keep operational claim status separate from revenue recognition, receivables, and cash so a submitted or accepted request cannot automatically become an earned fee.
fields.example: Claim U-184 moves through draft, reviewed, submitted, accepted, applied, invoiced, and paid. Submission stores a counterparty receipt; application stores the credit memo and client statement. The engagement earns fees on accepted, applied credits, so acceptance alone creates no fee invoice. A denial records its own reason and supporting correspondence.

fields.name: Submission transaction and uncertain-response handling
fields.prompt: Describe the outbox record, request fingerprint, external receipt, retry policy, and reconciliation procedure for timeouts. Identify where human inspection is required because the counterparty cannot provide a reliable request-status lookup or deduplication mechanism.
fields.example: The system commits claim U-184 and its submission outbox record in one local transaction. A network timeout occurs after dispatch, so the attempt becomes reconciliation-required. The operator checks the approved portal for a matching account, invoice, and amount before retrying; repeated blind submissions are prohibited by the internal runbook.

fields.name: Evidence package and independent QA
fields.prompt: Define the minimum evidence bundle and reviewer checklist for each lane. Set materiality and sampling rules, preserve reviewer independence, and state which discrepancies prevent submission until the underlying entitlement or calculation is corrected.
fields.example: For an $8,400 tariff correction, the bundle includes twelve invoices, effective tariff pages, meter records, authorization, and a line-by-line calculation. A second reviewer checks all material amounts and filing dates. One invoice uses a later tariff version, so the package returns for recalculation before any external submission.

fields.name: Counterparty credit and client receipt matching
fields.prompt: Explain how accepted amounts, issued credits, client applications, and reversals are matched to claims. Specify treatment of partial recoveries, bundled credits, offsets, and unapplied balances before calculating the operator's earned contractual share.
fields.example: A utility accepts $12,000 but initially applies only $9,000 against the client's account. The signed terms earn a 35% fee on applied credits, producing $3,150 for this period. The remaining $3,000 stays in the unapplied-credit register, and a bundled statement adjustment is allocated using the utility's claim-level explanation.

fields.name: Fee invoice, payment allocation, and reversal
fields.prompt: Specify the fee calculation, invoice evidence, payment matching rules, and correction procedure. Show how a later recovery reversal affects operator consideration and reserves without deleting the original claim, invoice, or cash event.
fields.example: Invoice F-208 bills $3,150 against claim U-184 and links the $9,000 applied credit. The client pays $3,150 with the invoice reference. If $1,000 of that credit is later reversed and the contract requires proportional adjustment, the operator issues a $350 credit note and records the reserve use separately.

fields.name: Deadline, denial, and escalation queue
fields.prompt: Assign ownership for approaching deadlines, missing documents, counterparty silence, and denied requests. Record escalation intervals and appeal evidence requirements without assuming that resubmission automatically extends a statutory or contractual filing period.
fields.example: A parcel billing dispute has a documented account-specific filing deadline on June 18. Internal review is due June 11, with an owner alert June 9. A June 13 denial triggers contract review and a reason-coded appeal assessment; the system retains June 18 until written governing terms establish a different deadline.

fields.name: Closeout export and reproducibility test
fields.prompt: Define the closing package, evidence retention schedule, access restrictions, and independent reconstruction test. Require a reviewer to reproduce client benefits and operator fees from source records rather than relying solely on dashboard totals.
fields.example: The closing package contains the source manifest, claim versions, submission receipts, disposition letters, credit applications, fee invoices, and payment allocations. An independent reviewer reconstructs $80,000 of client recovery and $28,000 of operator revenue. Any difference remains an open exception, and the export excludes employee screening records unrelated to the utility engagement.

worksheets.completion_gate: A reviewer reproduces one complete recovery and fee transaction from original evidence, confirms duplicate protection and uncertain-response handling, and verifies that all material submission exceptions have documented resolution before production volume increases.

worksheets.title: Statutory, Licensing, Contract Addendum & Compliance Audit
worksheets.purpose: Convert legal and contractual constraints into executable account-level requirements. Document practitioner roles, fee restrictions, state licensing, employment-credit timing, representation authority, carrier permissions, and evidence handling so each recovery lane operates within its actual jurisdiction, agreement, and authorized service scope.
instructions: Create a jurisdiction-and-service matrix before marketing specific outcomes. Identify the applicable statute, regulation, contract, tariff, licensed role, and responsible reviewer for each lane; broad authority to audit invoices does not establish authority to represent taxpayers.

Have the tax practitioner classify the proposed federal tax work and compensation arrangement under current law and controlling authority. Use Treasury Circular 230 requirements where applicable, preserve the written conclusion, and do not assume commercial contingency terms transfer.

Check WOTC hiring-date authorization, pre-screening requirements, state workforce certification procedures, and filing deadlines before screening a cohort. Preserve the actual submission acknowledgment and separate credit computation from the operator's authorized administrative processing service.

Attach account-specific contract schedules covering authority, exclusions, baseline methodology, fee earning, collections, reversals, and termination. Make the client responsible for identified source records while retaining operator responsibility for evidence integrity and agreed delivery obligations.

Record a dated reviewer, source version, and next review trigger for every material requirement. Refresh the matrix when a jurisdiction, service, tariff, carrier agreement, employment cohort, or compensation model changes instead of treating the initial review as permanent.

fields.name: Service and jurisdiction responsibility matrix
fields.prompt: List each offered service, operating jurisdiction, governing source, qualified role, and representation boundary. Distinguish administrative analysis from regulated representation and identify the documents that establish the assigned specialist's current authority.
fields.example: The pod analyzes utility invoices under the client's tariff and authorization, routes Texas property-tax representation to a qualified specialist, and limits WOTC work to agreed processing support. The matrix cites Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1152 for property-tax consultant registration and records the specialist's status, scope, and applicable exemption analysis.

fields.name: Circular 230 compensation classification
fields.prompt: Describe the federal tax service, practitioner status, proposed fee formula, and current legal assessment of contingent compensation. Identify the precise permitted basis or exception rather than assuming every refund-related engagement permits percentage pricing.
fields.example: The practitioner reviews 31 CFR §10.27 and relevant controlling authority before accepting any tax-credit percentage arrangement. Pending that review, the operator offers $100 fixed processing per completed file, subject to engagement requirements. Utility refund contingency terms remain in a separate schedule and do not determine the federal tax fee treatment.

fields.name: Tax substantiation and practitioner diligence
fields.prompt: Specify the evidence required to support each tax position, who evaluates eligibility, and who signs or submits tax materials. Link the practitioner's diligence duties to source records, calculation review, and resolution of contradictory information.
fields.example: The assigned practitioner applies relevant duties under 31 CFR §§10.22 and 10.34 when evaluating credit support and return positions. Payroll hours, qualified wages, certification, and related-party checks are retained with the workpaper. A recruiter spreadsheet alone cannot establish eligibility, and conflicting wage totals return to payroll for documented reconciliation.

fields.name: WOTC authorization, screening, and submission timing
fields.prompt: Record hiring dates, applicable authorization under 26 U.S.C. §51, pre-screening completion, state submission deadline, and certification evidence. Explain how the workflow responds when authorization for a hiring period or timely filing cannot be established.
fields.example: For a historical employee starting June 2, 2025, the employer completes the required pre-screening by the offer date and submits Form 8850 to the state workforce agency by June 30. The record cites §51(d)(13). Section 51(c)(4)'s December 31, 2025 hiring cutoff requires checking enacted extensions before later cohorts proceed.

fields.name: WOTC wage-hour calculation and processing boundary
fields.prompt: Document the employee category, qualified wage cap, hours worked, certification status, and employer-level limitations. Show an illustrative credit calculation separately from the operator's processing fee and identify who verifies the final return treatment.
fields.example: For an otherwise eligible ordinary category with a $6,000 wage cap, 400 qualifying hours support a 40% calculation, or $2,400; 120–399 qualifying hours generally use 25%, or $1,500 at that cap. Category-specific rules and limitations still apply. The operator's agreed $100 processing fee remains separate from either credit.

fields.name: Property-tax registration and protest deadline
fields.prompt: Identify the parcel jurisdiction, representative qualifications, client appointment, protest deadline, and evidence requirements. Use the applicable notice and statutory exceptions to calculate the actual filing date rather than relying on a generic annual reminder.
fields.example: For a Texas parcel, the representative checks Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1152 and appointment requirements under Texas Tax Code §1.111. The ordinary protest deadline under §41.44 is generally May 15 or thirty days after notice delivery, whichever is later, subject to applicable exceptions. The actual notice and filing receipt remain attached.

fields.name: Letters of Authorization and disclosure restrictions
fields.prompt: Draft the account-specific authority, permitted communications, delegation limits, term, revocation process, and evidence-sharing boundaries. Require baseline snapshots and signed authority before disclosing tariff findings or contacting the counterparty about recoveries.
fields.example: The authorization permits Harbor's named operator to obtain billing records and submit documented disputes for meters A104 and A105 through December 31. It excludes changing bank instructions, accepting settlements, and filing tax returns. The operator may share relevant invoices with the named utility specialist only under the engagement's confidentiality terms.

fields.name: Contingency and shared-savings contract addendum
fields.prompt: Specify eligible recoveries, exclusions, fee percentage, baseline adjustments, thirty-six-month measurement, payment timing, reversals, termination, and dispute resolution. Explain how incumbent claims and client operational changes are excluded from the operator's earned savings.
fields.example: The addendum charges 35% of accepted, applied historical utility credits and 40% of independently verified monthly savings for thirty-six measured months. It excludes previously filed claims, production shutdowns, and unrelated procurement discounts. Fees are due fifteen days after invoice; proportional credit reversals generate corresponding fee adjustments under the stated reconciliation procedure.

fields.name: Carrier access permissions and agreement hierarchy
fields.prompt: Record carrier developer terms, account permissions, available interfaces, rate limits, and submission restrictions. Explain how negotiated agreements and service-specific rules affect automation, including situations where only an approved manual channel is available.
fields.example: UPS billing exports are enabled for the client's account, but the available interface does not provide an authorized refund submission operation. The pipeline prepares reviewed evidence and assigns portal submission to an authorized operator. FedEx capabilities are evaluated separately; possessing account credentials does not establish permission to automate every account action.

fields.name: Sensitive records, tax information, and retention
fields.prompt: Define access roles, transfer methods, retention periods, deletion triggers, and incident responsibilities for client and employee records. Assess applicable tax-information restrictions and state privacy obligations according to the actual service and information handled.
fields.example: Employee screening records stay in a restricted workspace separate from invoice-audit exports. The practitioner evaluates 26 U.S.C. §7216 and 26 CFR §301.7216 where return-preparer disclosure rules apply. Role-based access excludes sales staff, retention follows the documented engagement schedule, and legal holds suspend deletion only for the affected records.

worksheets.completion_gate: The engagement owner and assigned specialists sign the dated service matrix, fee classification, jurisdiction checks, authorization schedules, and evidence-handling requirements. Each active lane has an identified qualified reviewer and no unresolved restriction affecting the planned work.

worksheets.title: Automation Pipeline, Acquisition Flywheel & Risk Fallback Tracker
worksheets.purpose: Automate evidence collection and repeatable analysis while preserving human judgment for entitlement, deadlines, and uncertain outcomes. Build an acquisition loop around verified recovery results, monitor integration permissions and error rates, and maintain practical fallback paths for carrier outages, OCR failures, and hiring-system interruptions.
instructions: Map each integration to a specific authorized task, account owner, credential scope, and fallback procedure. Evaluate FedEx and UPS interfaces independently, and treat refund submission capability as account-dependent rather than a universal feature of carrier developer access.

Separate ingestion, extraction, entitlement evaluation, review, submission, and reconciliation into observable stages. Give every stage an owner, retry budget, evidence output, and error queue so automation failure cannot silently convert incomplete work into a completed claim.

Automate utility tariff and cooling-tower meter extraction only after documenting the governing calculation. Pair OCR confidence with total reconciliation and physical meter evidence; an apparently precise reading remains unusable when its tariff period or unit is wrong.

Connect ATS events to WOTC processing through approved employment workflows and restricted records. Track pre-screening and state filing deadlines explicitly, prevent duplicate employee records, and stop credit-specific processing when the hiring period lacks verified statutory authorization.

Measure acquisition using signed qualified engagements and collected contribution, not raw lead volume or client spending. Reinvest only after claims clear evidence review, preserve attribution by channel, and use client-approved case studies stripped of unnecessary account information.

fields.name: Integration inventory and least-privilege access
fields.prompt: List carrier, utility, document, accounting, and ATS connections with their permitted operations and account owners. Specify credential storage, rotation, access review, and revocation procedures without placing secrets in workbook examples or exported records.
fields.example: The inventory includes authorized UPS invoice exports, FedEx account reporting, a restricted document repository, QuickBooks invoice synchronization, and Greenhouse hiring events. Service accounts receive only necessary scopes. The controller owns carrier access, payroll owns ATS access, and the operator reviews permissions monthly and immediately after contractor departure.

fields.name: Carrier EDI and permitted refund workflow
fields.prompt: Describe supported EDI or API inputs, account-specific refund capabilities, entitlement checks, and submission ownership. Include rate-limit handling and a controlled manual process when the carrier does not expose an authorized claim-submission endpoint.
fields.example: An approved EDI 210 feed supplies invoice lines where the carrier and account support that format. The pipeline identifies duplicate charges and attaches the governing contract rule. Reviewed claims use an authorized endpoint only when available; otherwise a named operator submits through the approved channel and records the receipt in the same ledger.

fields.name: Utility OCR and meter-evidence controls
fields.prompt: Define supported document layouts, extraction thresholds, tariff versioning, meter-unit conversions, and human review rules. Explain how the pipeline detects missing pages, changed layouts, impossible readings, and deductions unsupported by approved physical metering.
fields.example: The utility pipeline extracts gallons, meter dates, tariff codes, and sewer charges. A cooling-tower reading of 120,000 gallons reconciles to meter history before a deduction is calculated. Layout changes or unexplained volume jumps above the client's agreed threshold enter review; the engine never infers a qualifying submeter from an invoice description alone.

fields.name: ATS-integrated WOTC deadline automation
fields.prompt: Map offer, start, screening, certification, and payroll events to the responsible owner and restricted record. Define deduplication, deadline alerts, failed-event recovery, and hiring-date authorization checks before creating a credit-processing task.
fields.example: For the supported historical cohort, a Greenhouse offer event creates a pre-screening task; the start event creates the twenty-eight-day state submission deadline. Alerts fire on days 14, 21, and 25. Employee identifiers remain restricted, rehires trigger review, and missing authorization for later hiring periods prevents automatic credit eligibility assumptions.

fields.name: Rules engine versioning and release evidence
fields.prompt: Record rule owners, effective dates, source citations, test fixtures, and deployment rollback procedures. Separate tariff and contract changes from code changes so historical claims can be reproduced using the rules effective for their periods.
fields.example: Tariff rule UTIL-A-2025-v3 applies only to the documented service dates and meter class. Ten fixtures cover correct charges, duplicate lines, partial periods, credits, and missing readings. A reviewer approves the evidence before activation. Existing claims retain their rule version, while a rollback restores the prior rule for newly queued work.

fields.name: Operational telemetry and exception thresholds
fields.prompt: Define stage-level throughput, extraction accuracy, duplicate attempts, aging, and recovery-conversion measures. Set clear alert thresholds and owners, distinguishing a technical integration fault from a commercial denial or a missing client document.
fields.example: The dashboard tracks invoices ingested, reviewed claims, submitted claims, applied recoveries, and collected fees. An OCR exception rate above 8% for a document layout pauses that layout's automatic processing. Any duplicate submission attempt triggers same-day inspection, while claims without counterparty acknowledgment after the documented interval enter the operations queue.

fields.name: Acquisition channel and qualification funnel
fields.prompt: Choose a narrowly defined client segment and acquisition channel, then document stage counts, qualification criteria, acquisition costs, and responsible owners. Tie conversion to signed authority and reviewable evidence rather than verbal interest.
fields.example: A facilities-accounting partner introduces twenty multi-site manufacturers. Twelve attend discovery, eight supply sample invoices under confidentiality terms, four qualify, and two sign engagements with authorizations. At $3,000 total channel spend, acquisition cost is $1,500 per signed client. The team tracks later collected contribution before increasing partner spend.

fields.name: Proof-of-recovery referral and expansion loop
fields.prompt: Specify the evidence required for a case study, client permission process, referral request, and adjacent-lane expansion. Separate verified results from projected savings and avoid disclosing account details or employee information in acquisition materials.
fields.example: After an $80,000 utility credit is applied, the client approves an anonymized summary describing the error category and measurement period. The operator requests one introduction to a peer controller and offers a separately authorized telecom review. The summary reports the verified credit, not a projected thirty-six-month benefit presented as cash already received.

fields.name: Outage, waiver, and specialist fallback tracker
fields.prompt: Document the trigger, immediate containment, alternate workflow, capacity limit, and recovery owner for each material failure. Cover carrier access loss, guarantee waivers, municipal delay, specialist absence, and tax-substantiation gaps with distinct responses.
fields.example: If carrier access fails, the client supplies approved invoice exports while the team resolves permissions; deadline owners continue manual tracking. If a guarantee waiver eliminates entitlement, that claim lane closes rather than switching submission methods. A municipal delay moves collections forecasts, while a missing tax workpaper suspends only the affected processing file.

fields.name: Automation return and controlled capacity increase
fields.prompt: Calculate labor saved, review burden, implementation expense, and error-related costs for one automation. Identify the evidence required to expand throughput and specify how the team preserves reviewer capacity as input volume rises.
fields.example: Automating 1,000 invoice extractions saves six minutes each, or 100 hours monthly. At $35 per hour, gross labor value is $3,500. Subtract $700 additional review and $300 infrastructure costs for $2,500 monthly net value before implementation. A $5,000 setup cost pays back in two months if measured accuracy and volume persist.

worksheets.completion_gate: Every active integration has documented permission, an accountable owner, observable errors, and a tested fallback. One end-to-end batch demonstrates correct deduplication and review, while acquisition reporting connects channel spending to authorized engagements and collected operator contribution.

worksheets.title: 30-Day Launch Sprint, Pod KPI Scorecard & Exit-Readiness Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Launch an evidence-led recovery pod in thirty days without confusing setup milestones with collected revenue. Assign specialist ownership, measure cash and quality alongside throughput, and preserve transferable contracts, reproducible economics, and restricted diligence materials for future operator succession or a potential business transfer.
instructions: Use the first week to select a narrow recovery lane, verify specialist access, finalize engagement documents, and establish baseline controls. Budget within the $6,000–$35,000 startup range and retain the canonical one-to-four-month expectation for the first deal.

Use the second week for targeted acquisition and authorized sample reviews, not broad unsupported benefit promises. Define a qualified opportunity using documented entitlement, reachable decision-makers, usable evidence, and positive contribution after specialist costs.

Use the third week to process a small reviewed pilot through the complete ledger. Capture missing documents, deadline failures, and uncertain responses as explicit exceptions, and revise the runbook before increasing claim volume or extending the service scope.

Use the fourth week to reconcile economics, cash, delivery capacity, and client communications. Distinguish submitted claims from applied recoveries and paid fees; a successful launch may establish a qualified pipeline without producing a collected refund during thirty days.

Maintain exit-readiness as an operating discipline rather than a valuation promise. Organize assignability terms, customer concentration, rule ownership, contractor agreements, restricted evidence, and scenario reconciliations so another authorized operator could reproduce delivery and reporting.

fields.name: Days 1–7 foundation and funded scope
fields.prompt: Assign daily owners for service selection, specialist review, engagement documents, account authority, storage controls, and cash planning. Define tangible outputs and stop conditions that keep the launch within its funded and authorized scope.
fields.example: The founder selects utility invoice recovery for manufacturers, engages one tariff specialist, and prepares account-specific authorization schedules by day 5. A $35,000 funding plan allocates $4,500 setup and a $1,500 reversal reserve. By day 7, restricted storage, claim identity rules, and a weekly cash schedule are ready for authorized pilot evidence.

fields.name: Days 8–14 acquisition and qualification deliverables
fields.prompt: Set outreach, discovery, sample-review, and engagement targets with named owners and evidence requirements. Identify how unsupported opportunities are rejected and preserve the distinction between a launch activity target and a signed client commitment.
fields.example: The founder seeks twenty partner introductions, twelve discovery meetings, and eight authorized sample packages. Four qualified opportunities are a target, not an assured result. An analyst rejects two sites lacking historical meter evidence. Any signed engagement must include the correct client entity, covered accounts, fee schedule, and designated records custodian.

fields.name: Days 15–21 reviewed pilot execution
fields.prompt: Define the pilot population, reviewer assignment, evidence checklist, submission limits, and daily exception meeting. Require the pilot to exercise actual state transitions and reconciliation controls rather than merely demonstrating that extraction software runs.
fields.example: The pod reviews twelve utility invoices covering two meters and identifies three supportable billing corrections. A second reviewer checks all three before the authorized operator submits them. One deliberately repeated intake file confirms duplicate detection; no repeated external claim is sent. The daily meeting assigns owners to missing acknowledgments and calculation questions.

fields.name: Days 22–30 reconciliation and next-month decision
fields.prompt: Record completed launch outputs, open claims, cash remaining, unresolved risks, and the next thirty-day capacity decision. Evaluate progress against documented readiness and evidence quality without treating pending recoveries as earned owner profit.
fields.example: At day 30, three reviewed claims are submitted, none has yet produced an applied credit, and operator fee revenue from those claims remains zero. The team reports this plainly while maintaining the one-to-four-month first-deal expectation. Next-month spending is limited to funded commitments and additional opportunities meeting the qualification checklist.

fields.name: Pod roles, contractor capacity, and escalation ownership
fields.prompt: Assign accountable ownership for sales, analysis, specialist judgment, quality review, submission, billing, and collections. Translate headcount into scheduled hours and coverage without equating a contractor relationship to a full-time delivery allocation.
fields.example: The Base pod has one full-time founder and three contractors covering tariff expertise, document analysis, and independent review with tax-processing coordination. Their planned weekly allocations are twelve, twenty, and ten hours. The founder owns collections and substitutes only within their competence; regulated specialist work waits for an appropriately qualified replacement.

fields.name: Weekly operational and cash KPI definitions
fields.prompt: Define each KPI's numerator, denominator, measurement date, source, and owner. Include evidence completeness, review accuracy, submission timeliness, applied recovery, collected fees, receivables aging, and runway so volume cannot conceal deteriorating cash or quality.
fields.example: Evidence completeness equals fully supported claims divided by claims entering review; 18 of 20 yields 90%. On-time submission equals timely eligible submissions divided by submissions due; 9 of 10 yields 90%. Collected fees include matched cash only, and runway divides unrestricted operator cash by the forward monthly cash requirement.

fields.name: Canonical owner-profit and staffing scorecard
fields.prompt: Record the canonical annual comparisons and identify the separate actual-period reporting columns. Preserve the stated margin and staffing assumptions while preventing early pilot results, annualized pipeline estimates, or client benefits from replacing recognized revenue.
fields.example: The comparison retains Conservative $110,000 revenue and $33,000 profit at 30%; Base $505,000 and $217,150 at 43.0%; Scaled $900,000 and $504,000 at 56%. Conservative and Base use one full-time employee plus three contractors; Scaled uses two plus four. Actual results occupy a separate dated ledger and never overwrite these canonical benchmarks.

fields.name: Risk concentration, reserve review, and cash intervention
fields.prompt: Measure exposure by client, counterparty, recovery lane, specialist, and collection date. Define interventions for concentration or reserve shortfalls using cash and evidence thresholds rather than relying on aggregate projected recovery value.
fields.example: If one municipality represents $42,000 of $60,000 pending operator fees, counterparty concentration is 70%. The founder pauses discretionary acquisition when unrestricted cash falls below six weeks of committed spending. A new $2,200 reversal exposure exceeds the $1,500 reserve by $700, prompting a documented cash allocation and updated weekly collection forecast.

fields.name: Transferability and restricted diligence ledger
fields.prompt: Inventory contract assignment terms, client permissions, software ownership, rule documentation, specialist agreements, and evidence access restrictions. Explain how a potential successor receives enough information to evaluate operations without unauthorized disclosure of client or employee records.
fields.example: The ledger marks each engagement's assignment clause and required client action, documents ownership of internally written extraction rules, and links contractor confidentiality and work-product terms. A prospective successor first receives aggregated revenue, aging, and concentration schedules. Account-level files and employee records remain restricted until an authorized transaction process permits the specific disclosure.

fields.name: Founder independence and reproducible handover test
fields.prompt: Design a timed handover exercise covering qualification, claim review, submission reconciliation, invoicing, and management reporting. Record failures, remediation owners, and evidence that another authorized operator can reproduce the work without undocumented founder judgment.
fields.example: An authorized backup receives one closed utility case and reconstructs its $80,000 applied recovery, 35% fee, $28,000 invoice, and matched payment within two hours. They also locate the governing tariff and authorization without founder assistance. A missing baseline adjustment explanation becomes a remediation item; the exercise repeats after the runbook and evidence index are corrected.

worksheets.completion_gate: The founder signs a thirty-day closeout showing completed outputs, open exceptions, unrestricted cash, assigned pod capacity, and accurate claim-to-fee reporting. An authorized backup completes the handover test, and the next sprint proceeds only within documented authority and funded commitments.
